partition_main: Dirichlet alpha=0.5, 10 clients per domain, drawn separately in each domain with the run seed; cross-silo clients = union of the two within-domain client sets (identical clients)
partition_excluded: source-IP clients: enterprise sample has 23 source IPs, 9 of 10 IP clients hold a single class
H1: cross-domain transfer loses >= 10 pp macro-F1 in both directions (centralised FA-MLP)
H2: kept as stated: cross-silo FedAvg raises each domain test macro-F1 by >= 1 pp over within-domain FedAvg (Holm p<0.05)
H2b_added: non-inferiority: cross-silo FedAvg is within 1 pp of within-domain FedAvg on each domain (TOST, alpha 0.05, 10 paired seeds). Added after the centralised references (pooling: +0.19 pp IoT; enterprise at 0.9993 ceiling), before any federated run.
H3: under cross-silo training, at least one of FedProx/SCAFFOLD/FedDyn exceeds FedAvg (paired t, Holm)
H4: rule ranking differs between within-domain and cross-silo training
lr_selection: seed 42, random split, Dirichlet 0.5, VALIDATION only (test not computed): mean of val macro-F1 over rounds 80/90/100; cross-silo = mean of the two domains; chosen per rule and per setting; FedProx uses the FedAvg lr; differences < 0.0005 go to the smaller lr; the same lr is used on the time split
score: test macro-F1 averaged over rounds 80/90/100, per domain
